RHODE ISLAND PARCC 2016 SGP ANALYSES

Damian W Betebenner
National Center for the Improvement of Educational Assessment
Dover, NH June 13th, 2016

BACKGROUND

• 2016 SGP analyses of Rhode Island PARCC data were
conducted in December, 2016

• Analyses were conducted using PARCC scale scores (instead
of theta values) and scale scores for prior NECAP.

• Of the 4 PARCC states we work with on SGP analyses, 3
are using theta values.

• Pearson will return SGPs calculated using theta values.

SGP BASICS
• SGPs can be calculated using 1 or more prior scores.

• Analyses run by all states use multiple priors, when available, sometimes up to the
maximum available # of priors.

• SGPs, regardless of number of priors used are uncorrelated with initial achievement
(i.e. the 1st prior).

• SGPs are uncorrelated from year to year.

• Even though individual level SGPs are uncorrelated with prior achievement, that
doesn’t mean aggregates of SGPs (e.g., median SGP at school level) are uncorrelated
with prior achievement.

• median SGPs can be correlated with prior achievement because of actual
differences in schools, measurement error.

AGGREGATE SGPS

• The purpose of these analyses was to investigate school level SGPs using 1 and 2
priors.

• PARCC analyses will utilize a single prior (all they have) whereas Rhode Island can
calculate SGPs using more than a single prior. (Again, PARCC will calculate using
thetas.)

• Multiple priors reduces the impact of measurement error in the calculation of SGPs.

• This, in turn, will reduce the correlation observed between the beginning
achievement level of groups of students and the average growth of those students.
